skill.name: neurokit2
skill.description: Comprehensive NeuroKit2 guide for processing physiological signals including ECG, EEG, EDA, RSP, PPG, EMG, and EOG. Use it for biosignal preprocessing, quality checks, HRV, event-related analysis, complexity metrics, and multimodal physiological research workflows.
skill.summary: Guides NeuroKit2 workflows for multimodal biosignal processing and physiological signal analysis.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by scientific prose, Markdown inline code, and fenced examples. One low-risk network item remains for the mutable development install URL, and one medium semantic issue was added for promotional steering to an external hosted platform.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted platform
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive K-Dense Web promotion from SKILL.md or move it to a neutral resource note shown only when directly requested.
Prefer the standard PyPI installation guidance, and pin any development URL to a trusted commit if it must remain documented.

content.value_statement: Biosignal analysis requires careful preprocessing, validated metrics, and modality-specific methods. This skill guides NeuroKit2 workflows for ECG, EEG, EDA, RSP, PPG, EMG, EOG, HRV, events, and complexity.
actual_capabilities: Guides ECG and PPG cleaning, peak detection, delineation, pulse analysis, and HRV workflows.
Supports EEG band power, microstate, source localization, and complexity analysis guidance.
Explains EDA, RSP, EMG, and EOG processing pipelines with NeuroKit2 functions.
Helps choose event-related or interval-related analysis modes from recording duration.
Documents entropy, fractal, nonlinear dynamics, and general signal processing utilities.
Supports multimodal processing with bio_process and bio_analyze workflow guidance.
limitations: Does not validate clinical diagnoses or replace regulated medical review.
Requires user-provided data, sampling rates, event markers, and modality context.
Depends on NeuroKit2 and compatible Python packages being available in the environment.
Quality depends on sensor placement, artifacts, and preprocessing choices.

use_cases.title: Plan a Psychophysiology Study
use_cases.description: Map ECG, EDA, RSP, and event markers into a clear NeuroKit2 preprocessing and analysis workflow.

use_cases.title: Review Wearable Signal Quality
use_cases.description: Choose quality checks, filters, and HRV or pulse metrics for PPG and ECG recordings.

use_cases.title: Analyze Multimodal Experiments
use_cases.description: Coordinate cardiac, respiratory, electrodermal, muscle, and eye movement signals in one analysis plan.

prompt_templates.title: Process One ECG Recording
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single cardiac signal.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an ECG recording sampled at [rate] Hz for [duration]. Guide me through NeuroKit2 preprocessing, R-peak detection, HRV metrics, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Signal Modalities
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for several synchronized signals.
prompt_templates.prompt: I collected ECG, EDA, and RSP during [task]. Recommend a NeuroKit2 workflow for cleaning, synchronizing, analyzing, and summarizing each modality.

prompt_templates.title: Build Event-Related Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: I have physiological signals with event markers at [marker description]. Design an epoching and baseline-correction plan using NeuroKit2 methods.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Complex Dynamics
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for nonlinear and fractal metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess which entropy, fractal, DFA, and nonlinear metrics fit my [signal type] data, [sampling rate], [duration], and research question.

output_examples.input: A 60-second ECG recording sampled at 1000 Hz needs HRV analysis.
output_examples.output: A workflow recommending ECG cleaning, R-peak detection, signal quality checks, HRV time-domain metrics, and visual inspection points.

output_examples.input: A task study includes ECG, EDA, RSP, and stimulus markers.
output: Suggested synchronized preprocessing for each modality.
Epoch creation around stimulus markers with baseline correction.
Separate event-related outputs for cardiac, skin conductance, and respiration responses.

output_examples.input: A researcher wants complexity metrics for resting EEG segments.
output_examples.output: A metric selection plan covering entropy, fractal dimensions, DFA, segment length concerns, and comparability checks.

best_practices: Always provide sampling rate, signal duration, modality, and sensor context before choosing functions.
Inspect signal quality and artifacts before interpreting HRV, EDA, EEG, or complexity metrics.
Separate event-related questions from interval-level summaries before running analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not treat NeuroKit2 metrics as clinical diagnoses without qualified review.
Do not mix sampling rates or modalities without documenting synchronization and preprocessing.
Do not compare complexity metrics across recordings with incompatible lengths or filtering choices.

faq.question: Can this skill process real biosignal files?
faq.answer: It can guide NeuroKit2 workflows after you provide the data format, sampling rate, and analysis goal.

faq.question: Does it install NeuroKit2 automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains installation options, but package installation should be explicit and environment-specific.

faq.question: Which modalities are covered?
faq.answer: ECG, PPG, EEG, EDA, RSP, EMG, EOG, HRV, events, complexity, and general signal processing are covered.

faq.question: Can it help with medical diagnosis?
faq.answer: No. It supports signal analysis and research workflows, not diagnosis or medical decisions.

faq.question: Does it support event-related experiments?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for events, epochs, baseline correction, and event-related physiological responses.

faq.question: What information should I include in prompts?
faq.answer: Include signal type, sampling rate, duration, sensors, task design, artifacts, and target metrics.
